bug_semantics: SimpleGCMConfig.getSecretKeySaltGenerator() falls back to org.jasypt.salt.ZeroSaltGenerator (16-byte all-zero salt) whenever jasypt.encryptor.gcm-secret-key-salt is unset. SimpleGCMByteEncryptor.loadSecretKey then feeds that salt into PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 (getAESKeyFromPassword / PBEKeySpec) to derive the AES-256 key, so every deployment that shares a master password derives a byte-identical key. Captured GCM ciphertext from one environment decrypts on any other with the same password, and a single rainbow table applies worldwide (CWE-760/CWE-759, plus CWE-1188 insecure default). The default path is the documented GCM master-password recipe. A later same-branch commit also dropped the GCM iteration default from 65536 to 1000 (CWE-916), compounding offline brute-force cost, but the CVE/GHSA sink is the predictable-salt generator. CVE.org CVE-2026-9370 is PUBLISHED (VulDB CNA; not rejected). GHSA-jgj7-c8vj-w563 withdrawn_at is null, first_patched_version is null. Public history still has the ZeroSaltGenerator fallback at HEAD; GitHub issue #431 is open with no closing PR. Advisory range >=3.0.0 overstates 3.0.0–3.0.3, which do not contain SimpleGCMConfig; the GCM surface first shipped in 3.0.4 and remains through 4.0.4 / 4.0.5-SNAPSHOT.

potential_fix.approach: Remove the ZeroSaltGenerator fallback in getSecretKeySaltGenerator: fail closed with IllegalStateException requiring jasypt.encryptor.gcm-secret-key-salt, or generate a random salt and persist it with each ciphertext; raise the PBKDF2 iteration default from 1000 to OWASP 2023 guidance (600000) and warn at startup when salt/iterations remain weak.
potential_fix.rationale: A unique salt is a NIST SP 800-132 precondition for PBKDF2. Eliminating the global all-zero salt restores per-deployment or per-ciphertext uniqueness, so rainbow tables and cross-deployment AES key reuse no longer apply to default GCM master-password users.
